stock.name: stone
stock.note: Rock dug out of tunnels comes up as stone.

stock.name: candles
stock.note: Tallow and wax candles both count. Candles light the finer trades' rooms after dusk. {candles}

stock.name: ale
stock.note: Cups in the tavern's casks. The brewer brews grain only while food is above its plate.

stock.name: seed
stock.note: Each harvest keeps this much back for sowing; a hungry band may still eat it.

stock.name: flour
stock.note: Ground from grain at the quern or the mill; the baker makes it into bread.

stock.name: food
stock.note: Food counts meals, grain, oats, beans, cabbages, turnips, berries, fish and honey. Seed is kept apart.

stock.name: clothes
stock.note: Spare clothes and coats kept in store. People change into one when theirs wear thin.

stock.name: iron ingots
stock.note: Iron is smelted from iron ore at the smelter: {ore} iron ore in the store. There is no tool plate. The smith makes a tool when someone has none, or when a better metal is in the store, from the best ingots there.

stock.name: copper ingots
stock.note: Copper is smelted from copper ore at the smelter: {ore} copper ore in the store.

stock.name: tin ingots
stock.note: Tin is smelted from tin ore at the smelter: {ore} tin ore in the store.

stock.name: bronze ingots
stock.note: Bronze is mixed at the smelter: 3 copper and 1 tin ingot make 4 bronze. While bronze is short, the smelter makes the copper and tin it needs, even if their plates are at None.

stock.name: herbs
stock.note: Herbs are gathered from Bloommonth to Harvestmonth from wild herbs in the glades. A healer dresses a fresh deep wound with herbs while the store has them: it festers half as often. Herbs also make draughts for the sick, one a day for each who lies abed. When the store runs out while someone needs them, the colony lays out a herb garden by the sickroom.

mine.why: {Metal} is wanted ({have} of {want} ingots) and no open vein holds {metal}. This is beside the {word} seam found in a rock face: {far} tiles {dir} of the green, on dry, level ground.

waits.ladder: fewer than {logs} logs can be reached for its ladder
waits.far: it lies {far} tiles out and nobody free has gone to it
waits.nobody: nobody free is able to mine

places.magicWords: , where the air hums with something old

kinds.name: a spring
kinds.then: Fresh water to drink and camp by.

kinds.name: an old wood
kinds.then: Fellers can work it, however far it is.

kinds.name: a clay bank
kinds.then: Clay can be dug there for walls, with no mine.

kinds.name: a fishing pool
kinds.then: Anglers can fish it, however far it is.

kinds.name: a lookout
kinds.then: Whoever stands there sees twice as far.

kinds.name: a cave mouth
kinds.then: A cold breath comes up out of it.

kinds.name: a bear's den
kinds.then: Bones and claw marks lie about it.

kinds.name: a seam
kinds.then: Miners sink a shaft beside it and dig to the ore, however far it is.

list.what: an old coin, worn smooth, with a face nobody knows
a carved antler, the marks too fine for a knife
a cairn of stones that nobody here built
a bone flute that still plays one note
a deep blue stone, warm in the hand
a rusted blade from no smith they know
a standing stone with a ring cut through it
a string of glass beads in the moss
a ring of burnt stones where nobody camps
a pebble painted with a red hand
a carved owl small enough to hide in a fist

doing.thatch: Thatching a roof: a house without one lets its warmth out.
doing.mason: Masonry: a house wants stone walls, a slate roof or limewash.
doing.limeburn: Burning lime at the kiln: walls want mortar or limewash.
doing.fell: Felling a tree: {good} is set to {level}.
doing.scout: Out looking for {good}: the colony knows of too little.
doing.scoutHome: Coming home to tell of what they saw.
doing.scoutBeyond: Out to see what lies beyond: nothing new has been found for a season.
doing.prospect: Out looking for {ore} in the rock faces: the colony knows of no seam.
doing.search: Looking for {scout}, who is late home.
doing.quarry: Breaking up a boulder: {good} is set to {level}.
doing.carpentry: Making a {kind}: the {room} has beds for {beds} of its {sleepers}.
doing.carpentryBench: Making the bench: nobody can make furniture without one.
doing.goPray: Going to the shrine to pray.
doing.watch: Keeping watch by the fire at the fold until first light.
doing.goWatch: Going to keep watch at the fold: the pack has been near.
doing.cooper: Making a barrel for the larder.
doing.potter: Throwing and firing {what} at the kiln.
doing.potted: Carrying a pot to the granary.
doing.coopered: Carrying a barrel to the larder.
doing.shaft: Sinking the shaft: {good} is set to {level}.
doing.tunnel: Digging toward the {metal} vein: {good} is set to {level}.
doing.smith: Smithing a {tool} at the forge for {who}.
doing.hurtWeak: Lying weak from the loss of blood.
doing.draught: Bringing a draught of herbs to {name}, who lies sick.
doing.feed: Bringing food to {name}, who lies hurt.
doing.bury: Carrying {name}'s body to the burial ground.
doing.diedAway: Died at {time} {when}, away from the valley, and was never brought home.
doing.away: Away from the valley with {ill} until it passes, by the Sickness law.
doing.fold: Shutting the flock in the fold before dusk.
doing.unfold: Letting the flock out to graze.
doing.tame: Taming {a} {kind} from the wild {species}: the pasture holds {have} of {holds}.
doing.mow: Mowing the hay meadow after a dry night.
doing.mill: Grinding grain to flour {where}: flour is under its plate.
doing.feast: Going to the hall for the harvest-home supper.
doing.goStocks: Going to the green to sit in the stocks, by the Punishment law.
doing.stocks: Sitting in the stocks on the green, by the Punishment law.
doing.leave: Walking out of the valley for good.
doing.help: Working beside {master} at {skill}, as their apprentice.
doing.innkeep: Keeping the tavern for the evening.
doing.tavernDry: At the tavern, but there is nothing to drink.
doing.teach: Teaching the children at the schoolroom.
doing.lesson: At lessons in the schoolroom with {teacher}.

cellar.why: {count} roots and berries spoiled in the larder in four weeks

cure.why: {count} fresh meat and fish spoiled in four weeks

salt.why: Salt is wanted: {fresh} fresh meat and fish lie in the stores and none is salted. This is beside the {word} seam found in a rock face: {far} tiles {dir} of the green, on dry, level ground.

kiln.why: {count} grain and roots spoiled in the stores in four weeks, and pots would keep it
kiln.whyWalls: a house wants walls of a material the colony lacks, and bricks can be fired from clay
